definitions.explanation: Work assigned by a teacher to be done outside of class. A fundamental part of Japanese education.
Can also refer to something left undone that needs to be addressed, like 'homework' from a meeting or project.

examples.japanese: {宿題|しゅくだい}はもう{終|お}わりましたか。
examples.english: Have you finished your homework already?

examples.japanese: {宿題|しゅくだい}を{忘|わす}れてしまいました。
{毎日|まいにち}{宿題|しゅくだい}がたくさんあります。
examples.english: There's a lot of homework every day.

notes: {宿題|しゅくだい}をする means 'to do homework'. Japanese schools typically assign homework even during summer vacation ({夏休|なつやす}みの{宿題|しゅくだい}). The kanji {宿|しゅく} means 'lodging/home' and {題|だい} means 'topic/problem'.
